name: MonarchMenu
title: DropdownMenu
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu (popup, position, focus, back, motion) with Monarch rows: MonarchMenuItem, MonarchMenuLabel, MonarchMenuDivider
summary: A list of actions that opens from a control: MonarchMenu is the Material 3 DropdownMenu with a Monarch panel and rows (icon, text, shortcut, accent check, destructive tone).
whenToUse: For a short list of actions or options that belong to one control: More on a row, Sort, the actions of a split button.
whenNotToUse: Not for choosing a value in a form: use ExposedDropdownMenuBox. Not for content that is not a list of actions: use MonarchPopover. Not for a destructive action without confirmation: open a confirm dialog from the item.
api: @Composable fun MonarchMenu(expanded: Boolean, onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, offset: DpOffset = DpOffset(0.dp, 4.dp), content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)

@Composable fun MonarchMenuItem(text: String, onClick: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, enabled: Boolean = true, destructive: Boolean = false, selected: Boolean? = null, shortcut: String? = null, leadingIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
@Composable fun MonarchMenuLabel(text: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier)

options.name: onDismissRequest
options.description: Called on a tap outside, back or Escape.

options.name: offset
options.description: Moves the menu from its place next to the anchor.

options.name: MonarchMenuItem.destructive
options.description: Shows the row in the strong danger colour with the danger tint when highlighted.

options.name: MonarchMenuItem.selected
options.description: true or false for an option, with an accent check when true; null for an action.

options.name: MonarchMenuItem.shortcut
options.description: A keyboard shortcut at the end, 12 in the subtle text colour.

options.name: MonarchMenuItem.leadingIcon
options.description: An outlined 20dp icon in the muted text colour.

states.name: open
states.description: The menu appears below the trigger (or above when there is no room) and takes focus.

states.name: disabled item
states.description: DropdownMenuItem with enabled = false is drawn in the disabled colors and announced as disabled.

states.name: danger item
states.description: MenuDefaults.itemColors(textColor = MonarchTheme.colors.dangerStrong) for an item that deletes.

states.name: checkable item
states.description: A Checkbox with onCheckedChange = null as the trailingIcon, and the item toggles the value.

states.name: groups
states.description: HorizontalDivider between groups; a section title is a disabled item or a MonarchText.

appearance: A panel 192 to 352dp wide with 12dp corners, the raised background, a 1dp border (subtle in light, default in dark, strong in high contrast), a soft shadow in the light themes and 4dp around the rows. Rows are 48dp touch targets with a 40dp highlight (6dp corners) one surface step darker on press, hover and focus; text 14, icons 20 in the muted text role, an accent check for a chosen option, the strong danger role for a destructive row, the disabled text role for a disabled one.
platformNotes: The web builds DropdownMenu from Radix parts (content, item, checkbox item, radio item, label, separator, submenu). On Android: MonarchMenu holds MonarchMenuItem rows (selected = true or false for a radio-like option, with the accent check; the content overload with trailingContent for a checkbox item or a count), MonarchMenuLabel, MonarchMenuDivider, and a second MonarchMenu opened from an item for a submenu. The web item's tone danger is destructive = true; its shortcut is the shortcut parameter. iOS uses Menu.
accessibility: The menu is a focusable popup: focus moves into it and back to the anchor when it closes; back and Escape close it.
Every row has a 48dp target and the click action; a disabled row is announced as disabled.
An option row says whether it is selected; a group label is a heading.
Long text wraps at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: The menu scrolls when it is taller than the window.
Close the menu (expanded = false) in each item's onClick; it does not close by itself.
